Thanks for the thoughtful review, Mike. I bought an Asrock B580 Challenger for $330 in May. Here in South Africa, it was the best option at the time. Stuttering depends on the game but does occur, perhaps moreso in DX11 titles.

Chips and Cheese did an analysis and found that the driver is working in a different, possibly suboptimal way compared to AMD. I think the fact that Arc depends on ReBAR is indicative of the root of this problem: something to do with how the CPU accesses VRAM. Whether this can be fixed in the driver remains to be seen. But, as a B580 user, we must hope.

text: B580 user here, Rebar is indeed critical. Without it, you can lose significant amount of performance. It doesn't scale that well with older CPU's but its mile stones ahead of Alchemy. If we see this kinds of improvements, Celestial series will be very intresting. Yes, technology is immature compared AMD and nVidia. The biggest problem for B580's asides drivers that get better every update, is that production facilities do priortize AMD and nVidia over Intel, so Intel doesn't get B5x0's out it needs. There for prices for those that are available are insanely inflated. For MSRP B580 is a steal, but $250 -> $330+ range, not so much.

The only worry is the future of the Arc division, but since Intel will always need iGPUs, that gives hope.

text: If ever a company was the poster child for "you can't have it both ways" it's Intel. The GPU is a different beast to most other components in that drivers need regular and meaningful updates. There is clearly turmoil within the company about the lower margins because of the relatively larger die size. This may be true but the additional costs for driver support still need to be borne. Those costs are miniscule compared to what the product originally cost to develop. If they are not met then what was the point in the first place ?
